_doc: SSOT for the constants that space reclamation depends on. A value belongs in this file if, and only
if, MORE THAN ONE component has to agree on it — that is the whole membership rule. Single-consumer
numbers (Journal.creditGraceDays, the lifecycle rule's noncurrent_days) stay where they are used.
Why the file exists: these values were spelled out by hand in five places, and a mismatch was SILENT.
The daemon tags an object, the bucket's lifecycle rule never matches the tag, the journal credits the
user their space back, and the bytes bill for ever with nothing anywhere saying so.
Who reads it, and how each is kept honest:
- Terraform  — infra/coldstorage/root.hcl decodes this file into inputs; the module's variables have
NO defaults, so a missing value fails the plan instead of silently substituting one.
- Taskfile   — daemon:gate-test reads it with jq at run time.
- UI copy    — ui/src/shared/reclaim-constants.ts imports it; the delete-confirm sentence is built
from the number rather than stating it.
- Swift      — constants must be compile-time, so S3Store/Journal keep literals and
ReclaimConstantsTests asserts they equal this file. `task daemon:test` is the gate.
Changing minimumStorageDays is an AWS-facing decision, not a preference: it is Deep Archive's minimum
billable duration. Setting it below 180 makes us pay for storage the user has already been credited.
